_readme: Every piece of English prose on the site lives here so nothing is hard-coded in templates. Fields marked (md) in docs/EDITING.md accept simple Markdown (bold, links, lists). Names, dates, times, Zoom details and colors come from site.json; the program comes from schedule.json; the weekly meeting from meeting.json. Keep the voice warm and plain: we are A.A. members talking to A.A. members.

hero.headline: The Incredible Tapestry
hero.sub: A full day of weaving the Twelve Steps, Twelve Traditions and Twelve Concepts together, one number at a time. Free, on Zoom, with ASL and Spanish interpretation; open to every A.A. member, no registration needed.

intro.heading: Pull one thread and the whole cloth moves
body: Most of us met the Steps first, in a church basement or on a screen, from someone who had been where we were. The Traditions came later, usually when a group business meeting got lively. The Concepts, if we met them at all, arrived with a service job we did not quite ask for. We tend to keep the three in separate drawers. This workshop takes them out and lays them side by side.

**The Incredible Tapestry** is a free, all-day online gathering for A.A. members and anyone curious about how the Fellowship holds together. We will spend the morning with the Steps and the Traditions, the early afternoon with the Concepts, and the last part of the day in small breakout rooms, each tracing a single number through all three legacies. No registration, no cost, no homework. Bring your coffee and your home group's questions.

legacies.heading: Three legacies, one Fellowship
legacies.lead: At the St. Louis convention in 1955, Bill W. handed A.A. to its members in the form of three legacies: Recovery, Unity and Service. They were never meant to be studied apart. Recovery is how the alcoholic gets well, Unity is how the group stays well, and Service is how the Fellowship as a whole keeps the hand of A.A. there for the next person who reaches for it.
legacies.closing: Each legacy has twelve principles, and the twelve line up more closely than most of us ever noticed.

thirtySix.heading: 36 threads, one tapestry
thirtySix.lead: Take any number from one to twelve. The Step, the Tradition and the Concept that carry that number are three expressions of one idea, seen from the chair, from the group and from the Fellowship as a whole.
body: Look at the number **one**. Step One admits that we were powerless over alcohol and that our lives had become unmanageable. Tradition One says our common welfare comes first, because personal recovery depends on A.A. unity. Concept One places the final responsibility and ultimate authority for world services in the collective conscience of the whole Fellowship. Three sentences written years apart, and the same thread runs through all of them: none of us gets well alone, and the whole only works when each part admits it needs the others. Try it with **two** (a Power greater than ourselves, a loving God as expressed in our group conscience, the Conference as the active voice and effective conscience of the whole Fellowship) and the pattern shows up again.

The workshop is built around this pattern. The three legacy sessions each take one body of principles on its own terms, then the afternoon breakouts hand every room a single number to trace through its Step, Tradition and Concept. The same pattern shapes the planned weekly [36 Principles meeting](/meeting/): one number a week, all three legacies that week, read aloud together. The [study pages](/principles/) lay out all 36 for anyone who wants to keep weaving after the day is over.

whyAttend.heading: Why spend a Saturday on this

items.title: Finally meet the Concepts
items.body: Most of us have heard of them and few of us have read them. We will go through the Twelve Concepts in plain language, without the service jargon, so they make sense to someone whose only service job is making the coffee.

items.title: See your home group differently
items.body: The Traditions were written out of real trouble in real groups. Hearing how each one answers the Step of the same number tends to make the next business meeting a little kinder.

items.title: Work the Steps in a wider frame
items.body: Set Step Three beside Tradition Three and Concept Three and the thread is trust: trusting a Higher Power with our will, trusting that a desire to stop drinking is enough, and trusting our trusted servants with the Right of Decision.

items.title: Be in the room with the whole Fellowship
items.body: ASL and Spanish interpretation run all day, the room is open to any A.A. member anywhere, and the breakouts put you in a small circle with people you would never otherwise meet.

items.title: Speakers who have lived it
items.body: Each legacy session opens with a member sharing experience, not a lecture. Expect stories about sponsorship, group conscience and service before any theory.

items.title: Real situations, not case studies
items.body: The Traditions session works from things that actually happen in groups: the member who wants to record the meeting, the treasury that grew too large, the outside speaker with a good cause.

items.title: Small rooms in the afternoon
items.body: Mid-afternoon, after the Concepts session, we break into Zoom rooms of eight to ten people. Each room gets one number, traces it through its Step, Tradition and Concept, and reports back to the whole group.

items.title: Breaks, and a lunch that stays open
items.body: Two short breaks and a thirty-minute lunch. The Zoom room stays open through lunch for anyone who wants to keep talking; the interpreters take a well-earned rest.

howToJoin.heading: How to join
steps: On the day, use the **Join on Zoom** button on this page, or open Zoom yourself and enter the meeting ID and passcode shown here.
If Zoom asks, enter a display name using your **first name and last initial** only, the same way you would introduce yourself at a meeting.
Once you are in, find the **Interpretation** (globe) button if you want Spanish audio, or pin the ASL interpreter's video if you need sign language. Captions are under the **CC** button.
Settle in. Questions about Zoom go in the chat; the hosts will be watching it all day.
howToJoin.tip: Join a few minutes early if you can; the room will open ahead of 8 AM Pacific so you can sort out audio and interpretation before we begin.

schedule.heading: The day
schedule.lead: Eight hours, three legacies, two breaks, one lunch, and an afternoon of weaving it all together.
schedule.comingSoon: The planning committee is still weaving the full program; session titles and speakers will appear here as soon as they are set.
schedule.allTimes: All times Pacific. Your local time is shown automatically where your browser allows it.

accessibility.heading: Accessibility & interpretation
accessibility.lead: The hand of A.A. should reach everyone who wants it. ASL and Spanish interpretation run for the whole day, captions are available, and we are glad to make other arrangements where we can.

sections.title: ASL interpretation
body: American Sign Language interpreters will be on screen for every session, from the opening to the Responsibility Statement, including the breakout rooms wherever an interpreter is available. Interpreters rotate during the day and rest during lunch.

On a desktop or laptop, Zoom's **sign language interpretation view** lets you choose ASL from the Interpretation (globe) button, which places the interpreter in a dedicated, resizable window. If that option is not showing, hover over the interpreter's video, open the three-dot menu and choose **Pin**; on desktop you can pin more than one video so the speaker and the interpreter stay side by side. The host can also spotlight the interpreter for everyone when a session calls for it.

sections.title: Spanish interpretation (Interpretación en español)
body: Spanish interpretation is offered through a separate audio channel for the whole day. Interpreters render speakers into Spanish live, and when a Spanish-speaking member shares, the interpreter renders them into English for the main room, so sharing is welcome in either language.

To listen in Spanish, click the **Interpretation** (globe) button on the Zoom toolbar and choose **Spanish**. On a phone or tablet the same control is under **More** (the three dots), then **Language Interpretation**. Turn on **Mute Original Audio** if you prefer to hear only the Spanish; leave it off to hear the original speaker quietly underneath.

sections.title: Captions
body: Zoom's automated captions will be turned on for the whole room. Click the **CC** or **Show Captions** button on the toolbar to see them, or choose **View Full Transcript** to read along and scroll back. The captions are generated by software, not a person, so names, A.A. phrases and crosstalk sometimes come out wrong; please treat them as a help rather than a record, and remember that they do not replace the live interpreters.

sections.title: Other needs
body: This website is built to work with screen readers and keyboard navigation, and large-print versions of any handouts will be posted here before the day. If telephone dial-in is offered, the numbers will be listed with the Zoom details. For anything else, write to the planning committee and we will do our best to work it out with you.

accessibility.requests: If there is something that would make the day easier for you to take part in, please ask; the earlier we hear, the more we can arrange.

etiquette.heading: Zoom etiquette & online anonymity
items: Please use your **first name and last initial** as your display name, just as you would introduce yourself in a meeting.
**Cameras are welcome but optional.** Some of us join from a kitchen or a break room; you are no less present with your camera off.
**Stay muted** unless you are sharing or asking a question. The hosts will mute stray microphones gently.
**No recording, no screenshots, no photos of the screen.** This workshop is not recorded, and we ask every member to extend the same courtesy.
Use **Raise Hand** (under Reactions) to share or ask a question; the chair will call on you in order.
Keep the **chat** for logistics: Zoom trouble, interpretation questions, a dropped link. Sharing belongs on the microphone.
In the **breakout rooms**, let the host's prompt guide you, give everyone a turn, and come back when the timer calls.
Share the Zoom link within the Fellowship, in your home group, your district or your area, and please do not post it on public social media.

anonymity.heading: A word about anonymity
body: Anonymity is the spiritual foundation of all our Traditions, and it does not take the day off because we are online. Who you see and what you hear in this room stays in this room. Please do not record, screenshot or quote members by name, and if you share about the workshop afterwards, speak of what you learned, not of who was there. Members of this committee and the speakers appear by first name and last initial only, here and on the day.

seventh.heading: Seventh Tradition
body: This workshop is free, and there is no basket on this website. The members who are putting it together are covering the small costs themselves, as a Seventh Tradition contribution of their own. If the day moves you to give, please do it the way A.A. has always done it: through your home group, your intergroup or central office, your area, or the General Service Office. We do not accept contributions from outside the Fellowship.

meetingTeaser.heading: Keep weaving, every week
meetingTeaser.body: A weekly online A.A. meeting is being planned around the same idea: the Step, the Tradition and the Concept of one number, read aloud together, followed by sharing on how that thread shows up in our recovery, our home groups and our service.
meetingTeaser.comingSoon: The meeting day, time and Zoom details will be posted here once the founding group has settled them.

poster.headline: The Incredible Tapestry
poster.sub: Weaving the Steps, Traditions & Concepts together
poster.freeLine: Free · Open to all A.A. members · No registration
poster.footer: An online A.A. workshop with ASL and Spanish interpretation · aatapestry.org
poster.shareBody: Download the poster as a PDF or PNG, print it on letter or A4 paper, and pin it to your home group's bulletin board or pass it along to your district or intergroup. Both QR codes work from paper.

logoStory.heading: About the mark
body: The circle and triangle have stood for A.A. since the 1950s: the circle is the whole world of A.A., and the three sides of the triangle are our Three Legacies, named here the way they appear on a medallion: Unity, Service, Recovery.

Inside the triangle, three circles overlap like a Venn diagram, one for each legacy in its own colour. Where two meet, a Step and a Tradition, or a Tradition and a Concept, share a principle; the small shape where all three meet is the tapestry itself: the Fellowship, held together by all 36 threads.

contact.heading: Questions?
contact.body: Write to the planning committee and a trusted servant will get back to you, usually within a few days.

notFound.heading: That thread leads nowhere
notFound.body: The page you were looking for has moved or never existed. The whole tapestry is still here, though, starting from the front page.

footer.blurb: Made by A.A. members for A.A. members, in the spirit of Tradition Five: one primary purpose.
footer.editNote: This site is open source and updates itself from one data file.

share.heading: Spread the word
share.body: Tell your home group, your sponsees and your district. The best way an announcement travels in A.A. is still one alcoholic talking to another.
